correctness.rationale: The lengths define the exact short-arc fractions under the iid uniform endpoint model, and conditional chord rotations are independent and uniform. The arc symmetric-difference argument gives g(r,s)=2min(r,s); conditioning on a shared chord rotation establishes pairwise conditional independence even for indicators with one common chord, so both conditional moment formulas are exact. Independent integrations for Eg, Eg², and Var(E[g|R]) yield 1/3, 1/6, and 1/45; the overlap-pair count establishes Var conditional predictor n(n−1)(4n−3)/180. E conditional Bernoulli variance is n(n−1)/12. Total variance and L² optimal prediction prove the quoted explained fraction. The included verification source was actually executed and checked against geometric samples; finite tests are not the proof.

originality.rationale: The contribution is the exact conditional first and second moments of the full crossing count given the Euclidean chord-length vector and the sharp optimal-prediction explained fraction. In the primary full texts examined, classical exact marginal moments are explicitly recognized as prior; conditional geometric prediction is not covered. Direct overlap and synonym searches found no same claim. Residual risk remains from unlocated older integral geometry or a combination of standard conditional U-statistic facts, not from any located dominating theorem.
residual_risks: Generic Hoeffding projection and classical geometric-probability formulas could combine into the result in an older unlocated source; the search does not prove global uniqueness.
Flajolet–Noy marginal variance is prior and is not asserted to be original; original historical priority for the new conditional refinement is not independently certified.
Pre-2000 chord-geometry work may give the two-chord conditional kernel even if not the n-chord explained-variance calculation.

value.rationale: The question quantifies how much of a random chord arrangement’s topological crossing-count variability is determined by readily measured geometric chord lengths. The answer is an exact conditional second-moment theorem and a sharp optimal length-only estimator; its residual error is O(n²) against O(n³) total variance, so the explained variance fraction 1−15/[4(n+3)] tends to one. This is a motivated natural complete second-moment classification, not merely recomputation of the prior-known unconditional variance.
